title: Power limits and 60 m rules
blurb: The 1500 W and 200 W power limits and how they are measured, 60 m bandwidth and records, and new digital protocols.

G1C01.why: 10.140 MHz is on **30 m**, where the limit is **200 W PEP** output.
G1C01.trap: 1500 W applies to most other bands, not 30 m.

G1C02.why: 12 m has the standard **1500 W PEP** limit.

G1C03.why: On 60 m a USB signal may be at most **2.8 kHz** wide.
G1C03.trap: A 3 kHz signal would exceed the limit.

G1C04.why: On 60 m you must **record antenna gain** if it is not a dipole. No log of contacts or equipment is required.

G1C05.why: The 28 MHz band (10 m) allows **1500 W PEP** output.

G1C06.why: The 1.8 MHz band (160 m) allows **1500 W PEP** output.

G1C07.why: A new digital protocol requires **publicly documenting** its technical characteristics. Certification and experimental licenses are not needed.

G1C11.why: Maximum power is specified as **PEP output from the transmitter**, not RMS or antenna input.
G1C11.trap: Power at the antenna is after feed line loss.
